    by Louis van Wyk

    Fujifilm CodeBlue attains ISO 27001 certification for managed IT & security services

    News
    5 Oct 20262 mins

    Certification shows CodeBlue's information security management system aligns with ISO 27001 standard.

    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 1:58
    Instaread

    Fujifilm CodeBlue has achieved ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification for the information security management system which supports its managed IT, cyber security, backup, hosting and professional IT services.

    According to the company, which is a subsidiary of Fujifilm Business Innovation New Zealand, the certification independently validates the information security practices behind its managed IT and cybersecurity services.

    The certification, which follows an independent assessment, confirms that CodeBlue’s information security management system is established, operational and aligned with the ISO 27001 standard.

    This demonstrates that CodeBlue applies the same rigorous security practices it recommends to customers said Fujifilm Business Innovation New Zealand managing director David Jupe.

    “Customers, regulators, insurers and boards want more than a list of security controls. They want evidence those controls are governed, monitored and effective,” he added.

    “ISO 27001 certification gives customers greater confidence that the systems, processes and governance supporting our managed services have been independently verified.”

    The independent assessment examined governance, supplier management, incident response, business continuity, access controls and performance monitoring, Jupe said.

    The same governance discipline behind CodeBlue’s certification also informs how it helps customers manage cyber risk, said chief information security officer Mathew Jose.

    “Having completed our own independent certification process, we can bring practical experience to customers that need to strengthen governance, demonstrate that controls are operating effectively and give executives and boards greater confidence in how cyber risk is being managed,” he said.

    Many organisations understand the importance of cyber security but struggle to show that controls are working, responsibilities are clear and risks are being actively managed, Jose added.

    Through its RiskAware service, virtual CISO engagements and cyber governance advisory services, CodeBlue helps organisations assess their current security position, identify priority gaps and create practical improvement plans. This gives executives and boards clearer information for making decisions about cyber risk.

    “Cyber security is not just about technology. Organisations need a clear understanding of their risks, defined accountability and a practical plan for continual improvement,” Jose said.
